options.A: It works on each word alone: thousands of learned yes/no-style questions whose answers are added to its vector

options.A: Greedy decoding: the top-scoring token is picked every time, so output repeats
options.B: The model stops generating, because no token keeps a nonzero probability
options.C: Answers become factually correct, since only the model's surest token survives

options.A: It guarantees the same output every time, because the cut removes all randomness from sampling
options.B: It makes generation faster, since softmax only has to run over the few tokens that survive the cut
options.C: It shrinks the KV cache, since tokens cut from the tail never need their keys and values stored on the GPU
options.D: It cuts the long tail, so one unlucky draw can't derail a long answer, yet keeps variety among plausible tokens

options.A: Both set TTFT; TPOT is fixed by the model size alone
options.B: Neither: network latency dominates both TTFT and TPOT
options.C: Prefill sets time per output token (TPOT); decode sets time to first token (TTFT)

options.A: Prefill skips attention and only runs the MLPs, so it has less memory to read per token than decode
options.B: Prefill runs on the CPU while decode runs on the GPU, whose memory is slower to reach than the CPU's
options.C: Prefill reuses each weight it reads across every prompt token; decode reads all weights for one token per user
options.D: Decode does more math per token than prefill, because each output token must attend to the whole prompt again

options.A: Depth chains steps: a later block uses an earlier block's note (“it's a riverside”) to add one (“floods likely”)
options.B: Stacking shrinks the KV cache, because only the last block keeps keys and values for earlier tokens
options.C: Each block handles a different slice of the vocabulary, so 32 blocks cover more tokens than one wide block could
options.D: All 32 blocks share one set of weights, so depth adds reasoning steps without adding any parameters

options.A: Prefill and decode run on separate models, so new prompts no longer pause the decode loop
